name: SQL Server OTel Monitoring
description: Comprehensive SQL Server monitoring dashboard using nrsqlserverreceiver metrics. Covers golden signals, performance, memory, storage, waits, locks, security, transactions, query monitoring, thread pool, tempdb, and Always-On. Multi-instance support via instance variable (service.instance.id).

pages.name: Overview - Golden Metrics
pages.description: Critical golden metrics for SQL Server health

rawConfiguration.text:
### Overview - Golden Metrics

Key health indicators at a glance: how many users are connected, whether queries are hitting cache efficiently, how fast batches are processed, and whether deadlocks or blocking are occurring.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(sqlserver.user.connection.count) AS 'Connections' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.user.connection.count' TIMESERIES
SELECT latest(sqlserver.page.buffer_cache.hit_ratio) AS 'Hit %' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.page.buffer_cache.hit_ratio'
SELECT latest(sqlserver.batch.request.rate) AS 'Batch Requests/sec' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.batch.request.rate' TIMESERIES
SELECT latest(sqlserver.process.count) FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.process.count' FACET `process.status` TIMESERIES
SELECT latest(sqlserver.deadlock.rate) AS 'Deadlocks/sec' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.deadlock.rate' TIMESERIES
SELECT latest(sqlserver.processes.blocked) AS 'Blocked' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.processes.blocked' TIMESERIES
SELECT latest(sqlserver.page.life_expectancy) AS 'PLE (s)' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.page.life_expectancy' TIMESERIES

SELECT latest(sqlserver.cpu.count) AS 'CPUs', latest(sqlserver.computer.uptime) / 86400 AS 'Uptime (days)' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName IN ('sqlserver.cpu.count', 'sqlserver.computer.uptime')

pages.name: Slow Queries
pages.description: Detailed breakdown of the slowest queries

rawConfiguration.text:
### Slow Queries

Detailed breakdown of the slowest queries ranked by elapsed time, CPU, reads, and memory grants.

nrqlQueries.query: FROM Log SELECT latest(db.query.full_text) AS 'Query', latest(sqlserver.query_hash) AS 'query_hash', latest(db.namespace) AS 'Database', sum(sqlserver.execution_count) AS 'Executions', sum(sqlserver.total_elapsed_time)/sum(sqlserver.execution_count) AS 'Avg Duration (s)', sum(sqlserver.total_worker_time)/sum(sqlserver.execution_count) AS 'Avg CPU (s)', sum(sqlserver.total_logical_reads) AS 'Logical Reads' WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND event.name = 'db.server.top_query' FACET sqlserver.query_hash LIMIT MAX
SELECT sum(sqlserver.execution_count) FROM Log WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND event.name = 'db.server.top_query' FACET db.namespace TIMESERIES

SELECT sum(sqlserver.total_worker_time)/sum(sqlserver.execution_count) AS 'Avg CPU (s)' FROM Log WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND event.name = 'db.server.top_query' FACET db.namespace TIMESERIES

pages.name: Active Queries
pages.description: Real-time snapshot of currently executing sessions

rawConfiguration.text:
### Active Queries

Real-time snapshot of currently executing sessions: what they are running, what they are waiting on, which sessions are blocking others, and how long they have been waiting.

nrqlQueries.query: FROM Log SELECT latest(sqlserver.query_start) AS 'Start Time', latest(sqlserver.query_hash) AS 'query_hash',  latest(db.namespace) AS 'Database', latest(sqlserver.total_elapsed_time) AS 'Duration (s)', latest(db.query.full_text) AS 'Query', latest(user.name) AS 'User', latest(client.address) AS 'Host', latest(sqlserver.wait_type) AS 'Wait Type', latest(sqlserver.wait_time) AS 'Wait (s)', latest(sqlserver.blocking_session_id) AS 'Blocked By'  WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND event.name = 'db.server.query_sample' FACET sqlserver.query_start, sqlserver.session_id LIMIT MAX

FROM Log SELECT latest(sqlserver.wait_time) AS 'Wait (s)' WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND event.name = 'db.server.query_sample' AND sqlserver.wait_type != '' FACET sqlserver.wait_type TIMESERIES AUTO
FROM Log SELECT uniqueCount(sqlserver.session_id) WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND event.name = 'db.server.query_sample' FACET sqlserver.session_status TIMESERIES

FROM Log SELECT latest(sqlserver.wait_type) AS 'Wait Type', latest(sqlserver.wait_resource) AS 'Wait Resource', latest(user.name) AS 'User', latest(sqlserver.blocking_session_id) AS 'Blocked By', latest(sqlserver.wait_time) AS 'Wait (s)', latest(sqlserver.open_transaction_count) AS 'Open Txns', latest(sqlserver.query_hash) AS 'query_hash', latest(sqlserver.query_start) AS 'Start Time', latest(db.query.full_text) AS 'Query' WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND event.name = 'db.server.query_sample' AND sqlserver.wait_time > 0 FACET sqlserver.session_id, sqlserver.blocking_session_id LIMIT MAX
FROM Log SELECT uniqueCount(sqlserver.session_id) WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND event.name = 'db.server.query_sample' AND sqlserver.session_status = 'running' FACET db.namespace

FROM Log SELECT uniqueCount(sqlserver.session_id) AS 'Blocked Sessions' WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND event.name = 'db.server.query_sample' AND numeric(sqlserver.blocking_session_id) > 0 TIMESERIES

pages.name: Execution Plans
pages.description: Query execution plans with drill-down by normalized hash

rawConfiguration.text:
### Execution Plans

Query execution plans (ShowPlanXML) captured for top queries. To drill into a specific query:

nrqlQueries.query: FROM Log SELECT latest(sqlserver.query_hash) AS 'query_hash', latest(sqlserver.query_plan_hash) AS 'plan_hash', latest(sqlserver.query_plan) AS 'Execution Plan XML' WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND event.name = 'db.server.top_query' AND sqlserver.query_plan != '' FACET  sqlserver.query_plan_hash LIMIT 20

widgets.title: Plan Regression Detection (Queries with Multiple Plans)

nrqlQueries.query: FROM Log SELECT uniqueCount(sqlserver.query_plan_hash) AS 'Plan Count', latest(db.query.full_text) AS 'Query', latest(db.namespace) AS 'Database' WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND event.name = 'db.server.top_query' AND sqlserver.query_plan IS NOT NULL FACET sqlserver.query_hash LIMIT 20

rawConfiguration.text:
### Performance & Compilation

Query compilation efficiency: how often SQL Server needs to compile new plans, whether it is reusing cached plans, and how often full table scans happen instead of index seeks. High compilations or full scans indicate missing indexes or query issues.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(sqlserver.batch.sql_compilation.rate) AS 'Compilations/sec' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.batch.sql_compilation.rate' TIMESERIES

SELECT latest(sqlserver.batch.sql_recompilation.rate) AS 'Recompilations/sec' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.batch.sql_recompilation.rate' TIMESERIES
SELECT latest(sqlserver.recompilation.ratio) AS 'Recompile %' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.recompilation.ratio'
SELECT latest(sqlserver.batch.compilation.utilization) AS 'Compilations/Batch' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.batch.compilation.utilization'
SELECT latest(sqlserver.batch.page_split.utilization) AS 'Page Splits/Batch' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.batch.page_split.utilization'

SELECT latest(sqlserver.parameterization.rate) FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.parameterization.rate' FACET `sqlserver.parameterization.result` TIMESERIES
SELECT latest(sqlserver.database.full_scan.rate) AS 'Full Scans/sec' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.database.full_scan.rate' TIMESERIES
SELECT latest(sqlserver.index.search.rate) AS 'Index Searches/sec' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.index.search.rate' TIMESERIES

pages.name: Memory & Buffer
pages.description: Memory pools, buffer pool, and OS memory

rawConfiguration.text:
### Memory & Buffer

How SQL Server uses memory: target vs available, buffer pool allocation across memory pools, and whether memory grant requests are queuing. Memory pressure shows as pending grants or low available memory.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(sqlserver.os.memory.utilization) * 100 AS 'Mem Util %' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.os.memory.utilization'
SELECT latest(sqlserver.os.disk.size) / 1073741824 AS 'Disk (GB)' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.os.disk.size'
SELECT latest(sqlserver.memory.grants.pending.count) AS 'Pending' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.memory.grants.pending.count'
SELECT latest(sqlserver.memory.area) / 1048576 AS 'MB' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.memory.area' FACET `memory.pool`
SELECT latest(sqlserver.memory.page.count) FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.memory.page.count' FACET `page.pool`
SELECT latest(sqlserver.os.memory.usage) / 1073741824 AS 'GB' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.os.memory.usage' FACET `memory.state`
SELECT latest(sqlserver.memory.cache.object.count) FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.memory.cache.object.count' FACET `cache.state`

pages.name: Database Storage & IO
pages.description: Database file sizes, IO throughput, and latency

rawConfiguration.text:
### Database Storage & IO

Database file sizes, read/write throughput, and IO latency. High latency on writes may indicate disk bottlenecks. Transaction log growth events signal the log is auto-growing, which causes brief pauses.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(sqlserver.database.file.size) / 1048576 AS 'MB' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.database.file.size' FACET `db.namespace`, `file_type` LIMIT 20

SELECT latest(sqlserver.database.page_file.size) / 1048576 AS 'MB' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.database.page_file.size' FACET `db.namespace`, `page_file.state` LIMIT 20

widgets.title: Database IO (Bytes) by Direction & File Type

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(sqlserver.database.io) FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.database.io' FACET `direction`, `file_type` TIMESERIES

widgets.title: Database Latency (sec) by Direction & File Type

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(sqlserver.database.latency) FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.database.latency' FACET `direction`, `file_type` TIMESERIES

pages.name: Wait Stats
pages.description: OS wait statistics by category and type

rawConfiguration.text:
### Wait Stats

What SQL Server is waiting on most: lock contention, CPU scheduling, parallelism coordination, or disk IO. The top wait categories reveal the primary bottleneck in your workload.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT max(sqlserver.os.wait.duration) AS 'Wait (s)' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.os.wait.duration' FACET `wait.category` LIMIT 15
SELECT max(sqlserver.os.wait.tasks.count) FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.os.wait.tasks.count' FACET `wait.category` LIMIT 15
SELECT latest(sqlserver.os.wait.duration) FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.os.wait.duration' FACET `wait.category` TIMESERIES LIMIT 5

pages.name: Locks
pages.description: Lock analysis by mode, resource, and wait metrics

rawConfiguration.text:
### Locks

Active lock analysis: which lock modes (shared, exclusive, update) and resource types (row, page, table) are being held. High exclusive locks with long wait times indicate blocking contention.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(sqlserver.lock.wait.rate) AS 'Lock Waits/sec' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.lock.wait.rate' TIMESERIES
SELECT latest(sqlserver.lock.timeout.rate) AS 'Timeouts/sec' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.lock.timeout.rate' TIMESERIES
SELECT latest(sqlserver.lock.wait.count) FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.lock.wait.count' FACET `workload_group.name` TIMESERIES

pages.name: Transactions
pages.description: Transaction rates, longest running, and version store

rawConfiguration.text:
### Transactions

Transaction throughput and health: how many transactions per second, the longest currently open transaction (long-running transactions can cause blocking and tempdb growth), and version store activity.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(sqlserver.database.transactions.active) FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.database.transactions.active' FACET `db.namespace`

SELECT latest(sqlserver.transaction.longest_running_time) AS 'Longest (s)' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.transaction.longest_running_time' TIMESERIES
SELECT latest(sqlserver.transaction.delay) AS 'Delay (ms)' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.transaction.delay' TIMESERIES

SELECT latest(sqlserver.transaction.version_cleanup.rate) AS 'Cleanup', latest(sqlserver.transaction.version_generation.rate) AS 'Generation' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName IN ('sqlserver.transaction.version_cleanup.rate', 'sqlserver.transaction.version_generation.rate') TIMESERIES

pages.name: Latch Analysis
pages.description: Latch waits, superlatch activity, and wait times

rawConfiguration.text:
### Latch Analysis

Internal synchronization: latches are lightweight locks SQL Server uses to protect memory structures. High latch waits can indicate hot pages (many threads accessing the same data page simultaneously).

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(sqlserver.latch.wait.rate) AS 'Latch Waits/sec' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.latch.wait.rate' TIMESERIES
SELECT latest(sqlserver.latch.wait_time.avg) AS 'Avg (s)' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.latch.wait_time.avg' TIMESERIES
SELECT latest(sqlserver.latch.wait_time.total) AS 'Total (s)' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.latch.wait_time.total' TIMESERIES
SELECT latest(sqlserver.latch.superlatch.count) AS 'Active Superlatches' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.latch.superlatch.count'

SELECT latest(sqlserver.latch.superlatch.transition.rate) FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.latch.superlatch.transition.rate' FACET `transition.direction` TIMESERIES

pages.name: Thread Pool & TempDB
pages.description: Worker thread utilization and TempDB health

rawConfiguration.text:
### Thread Pool & TempDB

Worker thread utilization (approaching max workers causes queuing) and TempDB health: space allocation by category, file count (should match CPU cores for optimal performance), and page contention.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(sqlserver.thread_pool.workers.count) FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.thread_pool.workers.count' FACET `worker.state` TIMESERIES
SELECT latest(sqlserver.thread_pool.workers.utilization) * 100 AS 'Util %' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.thread_pool.workers.utilization'
SELECT latest(sqlserver.thread_pool.tasks.count) FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.thread_pool.tasks.count' FACET `task.state` TIMESERIES
SELECT latest(sqlserver.tempdb.space.usage) / 1048576 AS 'MB' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.tempdb.space.usage' FACET `tempdb.space_kind`
SELECT latest(sqlserver.tempdb.file.size) / 1048576 AS 'MB' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.tempdb.file.size' FACET `file_type`, `tempdb.file.id`

SELECT latest(sqlserver.tempdb.contention.waiters.count) AS 'Contention Waiters', latest(sqlserver.tempdb.data_files.count) AS 'Data Files' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName IN ('sqlserver.tempdb.contention.waiters.count', 'sqlserver.tempdb.data_files.count')

widgets.title: TempDB Allocation Wait Time (sec) by Page Type

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(sqlserver.tempdb.allocation.wait_time.total) FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.tempdb.allocation.wait_time.total' FACET `allocation.page_type`

pages.name: Always-On / Failover
pages.description: Availability Group and replica metrics (requires AG configuration)

rawConfiguration.text:
### Always-On / Failover

Availability Group health: replica roles, synchronization state, log send/redo queues, and flow control. Only populated when Always-On AG is configured on your SQL Server instance.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(sqlserver.failover_cluster.replica.flow_control_time) AS 'Flow Control (ms)' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.failover_cluster.replica.flow_control_time' TIMESERIES
SELECT latest(sqlserver.replica.data.rate) FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.replica.data.rate' FACET `replica.direction` TIMESERIES

SELECT latest(sqlserver.failover_cluster.replica.database.queue_size) FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.failover_cluster.replica.database.queue_size' FACET `replica.queue_kind` TIMESERIES

SELECT latest(sqlserver.failover_cluster.replica.database.redo.rate) AS 'Redo Rate' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.failover_cluster.replica.database.redo.rate' TIMESERIES

rawConfiguration.text:
## Note

Always-On metrics only populate when SQL Server has Availability Groups configured. If no AG is configured, these charts will be empty — this is expected behavior.

pages.name: Resource Governor
pages.description: Resource pool disk operations and throttling

rawConfiguration.text:
### Resource Governor

Resource pool disk operations and throttling, plus login/logout churn rates and attention events. Useful for identifying resource contention in multi-tenant environments.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(sqlserver.resource_pool.disk.operations) FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.resource_pool.disk.operations' FACET `direction` TIMESERIES

SELECT latest(sqlserver.resource_pool.disk.throttled.read.rate) AS 'Read Throttled/sec' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.resource_pool.disk.throttled.read.rate' TIMESERIES

SELECT latest(sqlserver.resource_pool.disk.throttled.write.rate) AS 'Write Throttled/sec' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.resource_pool.disk.throttled.write.rate' TIMESERIES

SELECT latest(sqlserver.login.rate) AS 'Logins/sec', latest(sqlserver.logout.rate) AS 'Logouts/sec' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName IN ('sqlserver.login.rate', 'sqlserver.logout.rate') TIMESERIES
SELECT latest(sqlserver.attention.rate) AS 'Attentions/sec' FROM Metric WHERE service.instance.id IN ({{instance}}) AND metricName = 'sqlserver.attention.rate' TIMESERIES

nrqlQuery.query: FROM Metric SELECT uniques(service.instance.id) WHERE metricName = 'sqlserver.user.connection.count'
